tests.name: test_warmup
tests.description: During warm-up the rate rises evenly from 0.

tests.name: test_after_warmup
tests.description: From the end of warm-up on, the rate holds at the peak.

tests.name: test_settings
tests.description: Other peaks and warm-ups, given by position or by name.
tests.message: lr_at(50, peak=0.01, warmup=100) is 5e-05, but halfway through a warm-up of 100 steps to 0.01 the rate is 0.005.

tests.name: test_update
tests.description: update is the rate at the step times the clipped gradient.

tests.name: test_update_uses_the_functions
tests.description: update is built from calls of lr_at and clip.

tests.name: test_other_numbers
tests.description: The mean of other pairs, negative numbers included.

tests.name: test_silent
tests.description: mean prints nothing, so that it can be called anywhere.
tests.message: mean(2.0, 6.0) printed '4.0\n'. Return the mean, and print it where a person needs to see it.

tests.name: test_script
tests.description: The script prints the distance from the centre.

tests.name: test_defined
tests.description: There is a function called smoothed.

tests.name: test_values
tests.description: smoothed moves previous a tenth of the way towards loss.

tests.name: test_pure
tests.description: smoothed leaves the main program's smooth alone, and uses only its arguments.
tests.message: Calling smoothed changed the main program's smooth. Return the new value instead, and let the loop assign it.

tests.name: test_script
tests.description: The script still ends with the smoothed loss, for other losses too.

tests.name: test_halving
tests.description: Halving from 1.0 down to 0.001 takes 10 steps.
tests.message: steps_to(0.001, 1.0, 0.5) gave None. Does the function return its count, or only print it?

tests.name: test_other_schedules
tests.description: Other starts and factors give their own counts.
tests.message: steps_to(1.0, 4.0, 0.9) is None, but a value of 4.0 multiplied by 0.9 at each step first reaches 1.0 or below after 14 steps.

tests.name: test_already_there
tests.description: A start at or below the target takes no steps.
tests.message: steps_to(4.0, 4.0, 0.9) is None, but 4.0 is not above 4.0, so no step is needed.

tests.name: test_same_twice
tests.description: Calling it twice with the same arguments gives the same count.

tests.name: test_silent
tests.description: steps_to prints nothing; the caller prints if it needs to.
tests.message: steps_to printed '2\n'. Return the count and leave the printing to the caller.
